text: The carrier consists of integer lifts of C, with pairing x·y/m. The hypothesis C≤C⊥ makes every pairing integral, exactly the criterion in [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4). Finite coordinates and nonzero modulus provide a full lattice; self-orthogonality is explicit, and no field or primality assumption is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L227) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L234) passes.
Packaging retains the original integer-lift carrier.
Packaging retains the normalized pairing.

Projecting the bundled integral lattice recovers exactly the integer-lift submodule P_m(C). The construction adds integrality and lattice proofs without changing its vectors. This is the rational carrier corresponding to the scaled Construction A lattice in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2); the self-orthogonality and nonzero-modulus assumptions remain visible. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L68) passes.
Membership of each integer vector is precisely reduction into C.

Self-duality supplies self-orthogonality and identifies the dual-code carrier with the original carrier, so the integral lattice equals its dual. This is the self-dual-code implication in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). The finite-coordinate, positive-modulus statement includes composite moduli and does not claim that the resulting lattice is even. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L299) passes.
The full equivalence confirms the converse under self-orthogonality.

The comap selects integer vectors whose coordinatewise residues lie in C; the map embeds those vectors into ℚ^ι. This is precisely P_m(C), the unscaled carrier in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). The definition allows m=0 and arbitrary coordinates; fullness and the classical real normalization are asserted separately under their required hypotheses. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L60) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Real.lean#L170) passes.
The carrier is exactly the image of integer lifts.
For nonzero modulus the actual carrier maps onto the classical real normalization.

Forgetting and restoring a ZMod m submodule preserves its elements and scalar action. The displayed inclusion therefore says every two codewords have zero dot product, exactly self-orthogonality used in [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4). This conversion identity also holds at m=0; it does not assert an integral Construction A lattice there. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L211) passes.
For nonzero modulus this inclusion is exactly lattice integrality.

Scaling the ordinary rational dot-product form by m⁻¹ gives B_m(x,y)=x·y/m. Under real coordinate scaling by 1/√m this becomes the ordinary Euclidean pairing, as in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). The documented zero value at m=0 is a total extension; nondegeneracy requires the separately stated nonzero-modulus hypothesis. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L135) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Real.lean#L125) passes.
The bilinear map evaluates to dot product divided by m.
Real normalization preserves precisely this pairing.

The form satisfies B_m(x,y)=B_m(y,x) because rational multiplication is commutative in every dot-product summand. Dividing by the same modulus preserves symmetry. Thus it has the symmetric pairing required by the normalization in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2), including the documented zero-form extension at m=0. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L135) passes.
The explicit dot-product formula fixes the pairing convention.

The carrier is a submodule of the finitely generated integer coordinate module and contains every m e_i. When m≠0 those vectors span the rational space, giving exactly finite generation and fullness. This is the lattice underlying [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)’s Construction A, with finite coordinates and nonzero modulus explicitly required. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L103) passes.
Every scaled coordinate vector belongs to the carrier.

For the supplied self-orthogonal linear code, the integral lattice is self-dual exactly when C=C⊥: dual carriers are the corresponding integer-lift carriers, and those carriers determine their codes. This is the unimodularity criterion in [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4). The nonzero modulus may be composite; neither evenness nor Type II is asserted. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L309) passes.
A self-dual code satisfies the forward construction criterion.

The left inclusion says all pairings of integer lifts from C are integral. Since x·y/m is integral exactly when the residue dot product vanishes, this is C≤C⊥, the criterion in [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4). The dual is Euclidean, without conjugation; finite coordinates and m≠0 are explicit. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L167) passes.
Integral pairings are exactly zero residue dot products.

Pairing with m e_i forces every coordinate of a dual vector to be integral. Its remaining pairing condition says its residue lies in C⊥, proving the literal carrier equality. This elementary refinement of [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4)’s integrality criterion uses the same x·y/m normalization, without assuming C itself is self-orthogonal. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L161) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L167) passes.
Pairing with the scaled coordinate vector extracts the coordinate.
Remaining integral pairings are residue orthogonality.

Evaluation of m⁻¹ times the dot-product bilinear map is x·y/m, exactly the rational translation of the real 1/√m scaling in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). The identity applies to all rational vectors. At m=0 both sides are zero by the documented total division convention. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Real.lean#L125) passes.
The scaled real dot product equals this rational form.

The bundled lattice retains the ambient form m⁻¹ times the rational dot product. Nonzero scalar multiplication preserves its nondegeneracy, so this instance has precisely the claimed property. This agrees with the Euclidean model in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2); self-orthogonality supplies the integral bundle, not the nondegeneracy argument. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L274) passes.
The same nonzero-modulus construction is positive definite.

The supplied self-orthogonality already gives P_m(C)⊆P_m(C)∨. The reverse inclusion is C⊥≤C by the literal dual-carrier identity and injective code-to-carrier correspondence, hence equivalently C=C⊥. This is exactly [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4)’s unimodularity criterion for positive modulus, expressed for additive codes with their canonical ZMod module structure. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L259) passes.
The bundled dual carrier is exactly the carrier of the dual code.

Every residue vector has an integer lift, and embedding integer vectors in rational coordinates is injective. Therefore inclusion of the two inverse-image carriers is equivalent to inclusion of the codes. This directly checks the carrier construction in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2); the elementary identity also holds for m=0 and infinite coordinate types. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L68) passes.
Integer-vector membership detects exactly the corresponding codeword.

The existential statement unpacks the comap and subsequent map: x belongs precisely when some integer vector reduces into C and embeds as x. These are exactly the inverse-image vectors in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)’s Construction A definition. The formulation introduces no preferred lift and imposes no unnecessary nonzero-modulus assumption. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L68) passes.
For a specified integer vector the existential criterion reduces to code membership.

The integer vector m e_i reduces to zero in every coordinate modulo m, and every additive code contains zero. It therefore lies in the inverse-image carrier of [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)’s construction. At m=0 this is simply the zero vector; spanning is claimed only later for nonzero modulus. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L161) passes.
For nonzero modulus its pairing extracts the indicated coordinate.

The submodule 1⊆ℚ is the embedded integers. Thus the left condition says m divides the integer dot product, exactly equivalent to its reduction vanishing in ZMod m. This proves the residue-pairing calculation behind [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4)’s integrality criterion, with nonzero modulus explicit and no primality assumption. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L211) passes.
Applying the criterion to all codeword lifts gives self-orthogonality exactly.

The rational dot product is nondegenerate, and multiplication by the nonzero rational scalar m⁻¹ preserves that property. This matches the ordinary Euclidean form after the normalization in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). The explicit nonzero-modulus hypothesis excludes the zero form; empty coordinates cause no exception to nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L154) passes.
The normalized form is also positive definite.

The dot product with m e_i is m x_i; division by the nonzero modulus gives x_i. This is the coordinate-detection step for the dual lattice in the normalization of [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). The nonzero hypothesis is essential, since at modulus zero the left side is always zero. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L183) passes.
Coordinate detection identifies the full embedded dual carrier.

An integer vector embedded in ℚ^ι belongs exactly when its reduction lies in C. Injectivity of integer-to-rational casting identifies any existential lift with that vector. This is the direct membership test for [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)’s inverse-image carrier and remains valid at modulus zero or with infinitely many coordinates. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L60) passes.
The full existential criterion agrees with the specified-lift formula.

Packaging leaves the carrier and form unchanged, so its embedded dual is exactly P_m(C⊥), not merely an isomorphic lattice. The coordinate-pairing calculation gives this refinement of the duality criterion in [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4). Self-orthogonality is needed to construct the integral bundle; the underlying raw dual identity needs no such assumption. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L183) passes.
The unbundled dual identity holds for every additive code.

Projecting the integral lattice returns exactly B_m, the ambient dot product divided by m. The integrality proof changes neither the ambient vectors nor their pairing. This matches the rational realization of [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)’s real normalization, under the displayed finite-coordinate, nonzero-modulus and self-orthogonality hypotheses. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L241) passes.
Its self-pairing has the same normalization.

For an integer vector z, the full self-pairing is (Σ_i z_i²)/m, obtained by expanding the dot product before casting into ℚ. This uses the full squared-norm convention in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2), not the half-norm discriminant convention. The formula holds for every integer vector, without requiring code membership. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L241) passes.
The general rational-vector formula specializes to integer coordinates.

The lattice norm is B_m(x,x), hence x·x/m for every ambient rational vector. This agrees with the full squared Euclidean norm after scaling coordinates by 1/√m in [Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2). No lattice-membership assumption is needed for evaluating the ambient form, and no factor of one-half enters. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Basic.lean#L249) passes.
Integer coordinates give the sum-of-squares formula.

Taking the supremum of Hopf ideals killed by every map gives their largest common Hopf subideal, consistent with [Milne, 3.10–3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). [The lifted-family generation identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/CommonKernel/Basic.lean#L305) checks the construction. It works over commutative rings and arbitrary index types; an ordinary intersection of kernels is not assumed to be a Hopf ideal.
After passing to the common quotient, the lifted family has zero common Hopf kernel.

Every generator of the Hopf-ideal supremum lies in each ordinary kernel, so the entire underlying ideal does too. This supplies the quotient-factorization condition of [Milne, 3.10–3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). [The actual factorization identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/CommonKernel/Basic.lean#L214) checks the conclusion for each family member, without requiring its kernel itself to be Hopf.
Each original family map factors through the chosen common quotient.

The forward implication uses containment in every kernel; conversely, a Hopf ideal killed by all maps is one of the supremum’s terms. This is the ideal-order universal property behind [Milne, 3.10–3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). [Uniqueness of the quotient lift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/CommonKernel/Basic.lean#L230) checks its factorization interpretation, with no finite-family hypothesis.
The factor through the common quotient is unique.

The subgroup defined by J acts on the normal subgroup defined by I through ambient conjugation, the action used in [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [The all-algebra-valued conjugation formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Basic.lean#L72) checks the order z·g·z⁻¹. Only I is assumed normal; J need not be normal and no smoothness or field hypothesis is needed.
Every value-algebra point of the action includes as z*g*z^-1.

The conjugation action supplies the semidirect product of [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61): its underlying algebra is (H/I)⊗(H/J), while its coproduct encodes the twisted multiplication. [The normal-factor point formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/SemidirectProduct.lean#L123) checks the interpretation. No trivial-intersection assumption is imposed on the two ambient subgroups; this is the external semidirect product.
The coordinate normal-factor map induces n↦(n,1) under the semidirect point equivalence.
The coordinate acting-factor map induces q↦(1,q) under the semidirect point equivalence.

The named object unfolds to the categorical coordinate Hopf algebra, so this comparison identifies precisely the same semidirect structure from [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [The represented multiplication comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Basic.lean#L228) checks its use and orientation. It does not identify the twisted Hopf structure with the ordinary tensor-product Hopf structure.
The coordinate product map represents categorical normal semidirect multiplication.

The underlying affine scheme of the semidirect product is the product of its factors, as in [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61); the images of their finite generating sets therefore generate its algebra. [The categorical finite-type proposition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/SemidirectProduct.lean#L66) checks transport to the named object. Only the two quotient algebras must be finite type, not H itself.
Finite type of the two factor coordinate algebras implies finite type of the semidirect coordinate algebra.

This transports the coordinate map dual to n↦(n,1), the normal-factor inclusion in [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [The point-equivalence formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/SemidirectProduct.lean#L123) checks the factor and direction. The Hopf map goes from semidirect coordinates to H/I; it does not represent projection onto the normal factor, which need not be a group homomorphism.
The coordinate normal-factor map induces n↦(n,1) under the semidirect point equivalence.

Transporting the categorical coordinate inclusion gives the map dual to q↦(1,q) from [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [The acting-factor point formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/SemidirectProduct.lean#L149) checks that it uses H/J and the right factor. Its image need not be normal in the semidirect product; no normality of J is assumed here.
The coordinate acting-factor map induces q↦(1,q) under the semidirect point equivalence.

The equation unfolds the chosen transport: first identify the named semidirect coordinates, then apply the map dual to normal-factor inclusion. This agrees with [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [Restriction of multiplication to that factor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L67) checks the composition orientation. The equality concerns actual Hopf morphisms, not just isomorphic source and target algebras.
Restriction of multiplication to the normal factor is its ambient quotient-coordinate map.

The acting-factor map is the canonical Hopf comparison followed by the coordinate map dual to q↦(1,q), as in [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [The multiplication restriction identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L94) checks this direction and factor choice. The equation uses the same conjugation action throughout and adds no normality hypothesis on J.
Restriction of multiplication to the acting factor is its ambient quotient-coordinate map.

Conjugation makes (n,q)↦nq a homomorphism from the semidirect product, as in [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61); the construction takes its coordinate Hopf map with reversed arrows. [The normal-factor restriction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L67) checks the multiplication order. It does not assert that multiplication is injective or that the two ambient subgroups intersect trivially.
Restriction of multiplication to the normal factor is its ambient quotient-coordinate map.
Restriction of multiplication to the acting factor is its ambient quotient-coordinate map.

Transport through the canonical comparison identifies the represented map with categorical normal semidirect multiplication. The latter sends generalized points to n·q, matching [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61); [its generalized-point equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/SemidirectProduct/Normal.lean#L158) checks this identification. Contravariance reverses composition, and the explicit local normality instance supplies exactly the required conjugation action.
On generalized points the map sends a pair to the product of its ambient components.

This is H modulo the ordinary coordinate kernel of the multiplication map, the image construction of [Milne, 3.13–3.14 and 5.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). [The factorization identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L74) and [injectivity of the second coordinate factor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L109) check that convention. Field hypotheses supply Hopf-kernel flatness; no equality with products of points over every value algebra is asserted.
The coordinate morphism factors through its ordinary-kernel quotient.
The coordinate factor from the ordinary-kernel quotient into the target is injective.

The product contains both factors; maximal Lie dimension and smooth connectedness force it to equal I, hence I≤J in ideal order. This is the comparison step of [Milne, Proposition 6.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=145). [The radical-candidate specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Radical/Maximal.lean#L50) checks its use. Only I must be normal, and product closure with this fixed I suffices.
The actual unipotent-radical candidate family instantiates the fixed-normal-member comparison with geometric connectedness supplying ordinary connectedness.
Nested smooth connected finite-type subgroup schemes with the reverse Lie-dimension inequality coincide.

Restricting (n,q)↦nq to n↦(n,1) returns the ambient inclusion of N, as in [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). Contravariantly, the composite is exactly H→H/I. [The categorical restriction identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/SemidirectProduct/Normal.lean#L174) checks this equation. It holds over commutative rings and requires normality only of the first subgroup.
Categorical semidirect multiplication restricts to the ambient normal-factor map.

Restricting semidirect multiplication to q↦(1,q) gives the ambient inclusion of Q; on coordinates this is H→H/J. The convention is that of [Milne, §2.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=61). [The categorical acting-factor restriction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/SemidirectProduct/Normal.lean#L192) checks the equality. No normality of J or assumption that the product fills the ambient group is used.
Categorical semidirect multiplication restricts to the ambient acting-factor map.

An element killed by the product coordinate map is killed after restricting to the normal factor, hence lies in I. Thus the scheme image contains that factor, matching [Milne, 3.13–3.14 and 5.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). [The restriction identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L67) checks the direction. The field assumption ensures the ordinary coordinate kernel is bundled as a Hopf ideal.
Restriction of multiplication to the normal factor is its ambient quotient-coordinate map.

Restricting multiplication to the acting factor identifies its coordinate composite with the quotient by J, so the product coordinate kernel lies in J. This agrees with [Milne, 3.13–3.14 and 5.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). [The right-factor restriction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L94) checks scheme-theoretic containment, including nilpotents. Normality of the acting subgroup is unnecessary for this inclusion.
Restriction of multiplication to the acting factor is its ambient quotient-coordinate map.

When both factors are normal, simultaneous ambient conjugation lifts through multiplication; equivariance therefore makes its scheme image normal, consistent with [Milne, 5.3 and 6.41](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=109). [The lifted-conjugation criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Image.lean#L143) checks the precise argument. The field supplies the tensor-kernel flatness conditions, and normality retains the full closed subgroup scheme rather than only rational points.
A lift of ambient conjugation through a Hopf coordinate map makes its scheme image normal, with explicit ring-flatness hypotheses.

The topology on X×Y is induced jointly by its two projections, giving the coarsest topology making both continuous. The source identifies it with the topology generated by open rectangles. This matches the standard binary product topology for arbitrary topological spaces, including when a factor is empty. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L52).

The sum X⊕Y carries the topology coinduced by its tagged injections, so a set is open exactly when its preimages in both summands are open. This is the usual disjoint-union topology, with tags keeping the summands disjoint even if the original underlying types coincide. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L48).

A subset of X×Y is open exactly when every one of its points lies in an open rectangle contained in the subset. Both coordinate neighborhoods contain the specified point, and the rectangle is contained in s. This is precisely the basis criterion for the binary product topology. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L446).

A set is a neighborhood of (x,y) exactly when it contains u×v for coordinate neighborhoods u of x and v of y. The displayed u and v need not themselves be open; they contain open neighborhoods. This is the filter form of the standard rectangle neighborhood basis. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L269).

The neighborhood filter at (x,y) is the product of the coordinate neighborhood filters. Its basic members therefore contain products of neighborhoods in the two spaces, matching the product-topology basis. The result applies to arbitrary spaces and underlies the coordinatewise criterion for convergence of any filter. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L249).

Two continuous maps f:Z→X and g:Z→Y give the continuous paired map z↦(f(z),g(z)). The coordinate projections of that map are exactly f and g, so the assertion is the forward construction in the product universal property. Their source is the same space Z throughout. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L139).

Continuous f:Z→X and g:W→Y induce the continuous product map (z,w)↦(f(z),g(w)). The proof composes each map with its domain projection and then pairs them. This directly realizes coordinatewise continuity for products while allowing the two input maps to have different source spaces. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L178).

The product s×t of two open subsets is open in X×Y. It is the intersection of the inverse images of s and t under the continuous coordinate projections. Thus the stated hypotheses give exactly a basic open rectangle in the standard binary product topology. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L245).

The product of two closed subsets is closed in the product space. The source proves this from closure(s×t)=closure(s)×closure(t), which becomes s×t under the two closedness hypotheses. Equivalently, coordinate projections pull back closed sets and their intersection is the product. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L568).

The product of two topological embeddings is a topological embedding. Injectivity holds coordinatewise, and the product of the source topologies induced by the factors is induced by their product map. Thus the declaration preserves the full embedding property, with no extra assumptions on any of the four spaces. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L606).

The product of two open quotient maps is again an open quotient map. The source checks its three defining requirements separately: surjectivity, continuity, and openness. Openness follows because images of basic rectangles are products of open images, and arbitrary open sets are unions of such rectangles. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L646).

The product of open embeddings is an open embedding. The source combines the product embedding theorem with openness of the product map; equivalently its range is the product of the two open ranges. This matches the usual inclusion into an open subspace, transported through the given embeddings. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L627).

The product homeomorphism sends (x,y) to (h₁(x),h₂(y)), with inverse acting by the two inverse homeomorphisms. Both directions are continuous by the product continuity criterion. The explicit coercion and inverse identities confirm the expected coordinate order and recover the standard product of two homeomorphisms. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L671).

The associativity homeomorphism sends ((x,y),z) to (x,(y,z)), preserving all three coordinates and only changing their grouping. The underlying equivalence is explicitly Equiv.prodAssoc; continuity in both directions follows by projections and pairing. Lean’s right-associated target X×Y×Z has exactly the intended parenthesization. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L701).

The commutativity homeomorphism swaps the two product coordinates. Its inverse is the same swap with X and Y interchanged, and two swaps give the identity. The source’s coercion and inverse formulas establish these exact maps, while continuity follows from the continuous coordinate projections and pairing. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L686).

Distributivity sends (x,inl y) to inl(x,y) and (x,inr z) to inr(x,z), with the evident branchwise inverse. The source constructs this homeomorphism from swaps, the opposite-side distributivity map and sum congruence. Open summands and the rectangle basis ensure continuity in both directions for arbitrary spaces. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L976).

A subset of X⊕Y is open exactly when its preimages under both tagged injections are open. These preimages are the two component portions of the subset. The criterion follows directly from the coinduced sum topology and matches the standard definition of open sets in a disjoint union. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L769).

A subset of the disjoint union is closed exactly when both component preimages are closed. Taking complements converts this statement to the componentwise open-set criterion, since inverse image preserves complements. The characterization applies to arbitrary subsets and arbitrary topologies on the two summands, without compactness assumptions. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L772).

A function from X⊕Y is continuous exactly when both restrictions, obtained by composing with the tagged injections, are continuous. This is the universal property of the disjoint-union topology. The two maps need no agreement condition because their tagged source summands are disjoint, even if the original types coincide. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L736).

The closure of s×t is exactly closure(s)×closure(t). A basic neighborhood rectangle of (x,y) meets s×t precisely when its coordinate neighborhoods meet s and t. This yields both inclusions directly from the closure and product-neighborhood definitions, with no separation or nonempty-set assumptions needed. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Constructions/SumProd.lean#L529).

Bounded below means that a lower bound exists in the ambient type. No minimum or membership of the bound in the set is required. The definition needs only a relation; for the empty set it holds exactly when the ambient type is nonempty. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Defs.lean#L42).

InfSet supplies a total set-indexed operation sInf, without asserting an order or any infimum law. Its own documentation correctly describes an operator class. Correctness as a greatest lower bound belongs to additional classes; empty and unbounded inputs therefore receive supplied values without a universal-property claim. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Defs.lean#L75).

A least element must belong to the set and lie below every member. This matches a minimum, rather than a merely minimal element or an external lower bound. Only the relation is needed for the predicate; its documented uniqueness assertion is explicitly restricted to partial orders. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_setofreals.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Defs.lean#L48).

lowerBounds collects precisely the ambient elements lying below every member of the given set. Bounds need not belong to that set or be greatest. The generated order-dual definition reverses the comparison correctly and remains meaningful with only a relation, including for an empty set. Compared with [the reference](https://twjudson.github.io/aata-files/aata-20250801.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Defs.lean#L37).

upperBounds collects all ambient elements above every member of the set. It neither chooses a supremum nor requires a bound to lie in the set. Its universal condition is valid for arbitrary relations; for the empty set every ambient element qualifies, as the usual bound convention requires. Compared with [the reference](https://twjudson.github.io/aata-files/aata-20250801.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Defs.lean#L37).

The infimum of a bounded-below set lies below each of its members. Membership supplies nonemptiness, so no separate nonempty hypothesis is missing. The theorem uses conditional completeness exactly on its valid domain and makes no claim about the supplied infimum of an empty or unbounded set. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/ConditionallyCompleteLattice/Basic.lean#L197).

Conditional completeness supplies suprema of nonempty sets bounded above and infima of nonempty sets bounded below. The class correctly keeps the two one-sided boundedness conditions separate and extends a lattice, without requiring total order. Values on inputs outside those hypotheses carry no extremal guarantee. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/ConditionallyCompleteLattice/Defs.lean#L46).

This class adds totality and decidable comparisons to conditional lattice completeness. It also explicitly identifies each unbounded supremum or infimum with the corresponding empty-set value. Those fallback conventions do not assert infinite endpoints or valid bounds, and the ordinary bounded nonempty cases retain their universal properties. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/ConditionallyCompleteLattice/Defs.lean#L65).

The extra inequality supplies the missing direction of join-over-meet distributivity; the reverse inequality holds in every lattice. Thus the class gives the usual distributive lattice, without boundedness or complements. Its own documentation states the chosen inequality correctly and its powerset-representation assertion has the standard lattice-embedding meaning. Compared with [the reference](https://math.hawaii.edu/~jb/math618/LTNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/Lattice.lean#L294).

A lattice combines binary joins and binary meets on one partial order. The inherited laws give their least-upper-bound and greatest-lower-bound properties, matching the standard definition. It does not assume a total order, distributivity, endpoints, or infima and suprema of arbitrary sets. Compared with [the reference](https://twjudson.github.io/aata-files/aata-20250801.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/Lattice.lean#L226).

A meet-semilattice provides a greatest lower bound for every pair in a partial order. The two lower-bound fields and the common-lower-bound comparison express precisely that property. No least element, join operation, totality, or arbitrary-set completeness is included; equality of the two inputs is allowed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.hawaii.edu/~jb/math618/LTNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/Lattice.lean#L70).

A join-semilattice provides a least upper bound for every pair in a partial order. The two upper-bound fields and leastness field match this universal property. Joins need not equal one of their inputs, since totality is absent; no greatest element or arbitrary-set supremum is assumed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.hawaii.edu/~jb/math618/LTNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/Lattice.lean#L56).

LinearOrder is a partial order with total comparison, matching the standard non-strict form of a linear order. Its documented decidability assumptions and lawful min, max, and comparison data are explicit implementation additions. Empty and singleton carriers remain possible; density, endpoints and completeness are not required. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/LinearOrder.lean#L60).

Every element is at most the maximum of itself and a second element. The generated dual theorem has the correct left argument and non-strict inequality, including equal inputs. LinearOrder ensures max is the larger input, so this is stronger structure than an arbitrary binary operation named max. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/LinearOrder.lean#L162).

The second argument is at most the maximum of two elements. The generated dual theorem preserves the right argument and includes the equality case. The result follows from the prescribed maximum in a linear order; no algebraic, metric, completeness, or nontriviality assumption is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/LinearOrder.lean#L165).

In a linear order, failing a<b is equivalent to b≤a. The reversed comparison is essential, and equality is included. Totality excludes incomparable pairs, so the equivalence is not silently asserted for arbitrary partial orders; the source proves both directions with the correct hypotheses. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/LinearOrder.lean#L117).

PartialOrder adds antisymmetry to a reflexive transitive relation. This matches the standard notion while retaining the inherited strict relation a<b iff a≤b and not b≤a. Totality is not assumed, so incomparable elements are permitted; empty and singleton carriers also satisfy the intended laws. Compared with [the reference](https://twjudson.github.io/aata-files/aata-20250801.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/PartialOrder.lean#L175).

Preorder records reflexivity and transitivity without antisymmetry or totality. Its strict relation is coherently fixed by a<b iff a≤b and not b≤a, as the documentation states. Distinct elements may be mutually comparable; this does not force an unintended equality or quotient construction. Compared with [the reference](https://math.hawaii.edu/~jb/math618/LTNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/PartialOrder.lean#L43).

Mutual non-strict inequalities force equality in a partial order. The theorem exposes exactly antisymmetry, with both comparison directions required. It does not assume a linear order or infer equality from one inequality, and it correctly avoids extending this conclusion to arbitrary preorders. Compared with [the reference](https://twjudson.github.io/aata-files/aata-20250801.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/PartialOrder.lean#L187).

Strict comparison implies non-strict comparison already in a preorder. The result is the first component of the required characterization a<b iff a≤b and not b≤a. Antisymmetry and totality are unnecessary, and no converse or equality case is inadvertently claimed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.hawaii.edu/~jb/math618/LTNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Defs/PartialOrder.lean#L79).
